newsitem.title: FRANCE: French budget to trim 0.2 pct from 1997 GDP - OFCE.
newsitem.headline: French budget to trim 0.2 pct from 1997 GDP - OFCE.

text.p: France's OFCE economic institute predicts that the 1997 French budget will be slightly restrictive to economic growth in 1997 and 1998 because income tax cuts will not completely offset planned budget cuts, financial daily Les Echos reported on Tuesday.
The OFCE forecast that the budget will trim 0.2 percent from gross domestic product (GDP) in 1997. The budget is expected to cause job losses of about 25,000 next year.

Les Echos reported that 55 billion francs in planned savings in the budget would restrict GDP growth by 0.4 percent while a 25 billion franc income tax cut will lift activity by 0.2 percent, resulting in the negative overall effect of the budget.
The French government is predicting 1997 GDP growth of 2.3 percent. There is no official forecast for 1998 growth.
The budget is expected be positive for 1997 consumer consumption to the tune of 0.1 percent but will subtract 0.5 percent from business investment, Les Echos reported.
